accuracy.where: The map, in order, line 43: "`/implement` builds test-first with `/tdd`". The same claim appears in the flow Scene caption at line 69 ("`/tdd` and `/code-review` run inside") and the Cheat sheet at line 349 ("`/tdd`, `/code-review` and `/pr` run for you")
accuracy.problem: The Lesson says `/implement` always runs `/tdd`. In 1.3.1, `/implement` calls tdd only "where possible, at pre-agreed seams", and tdd won't write a test at a seam nobody confirmed. On the short road (Fork B 'No') there is no spec, so `/to-spec` never checked any seams with you. The Lesson's own Other developers bullet (line 242) then reports that `/tdd` never ran in 173 sessions, and nothing in the body explains why. Line 45 warns only that the review can misfire. A reader will expect test-first building that may never happen.
accuracy.evidence: implement/SKILL.md:11 'Call the Skill tool with "tdd" where possible, at pre-agreed seams.' tdd/SKILL.md:22 'Test only at pre-agreed seams. Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam.' to-spec/SKILL.md:15-17 (sketch the test seams, then check them with the user). Lesson line 242: '`/tdd` had never run'. In GitHub Discussion #1136, Warshoow's 2026-09-29 comment says '/tdd never ran once'. [Implement](/learn/implement) line 52 already teaches this weak spot.
accuracy.fix: Line 43: "`/implement` drives `/tdd` (a failing check first, then the code that passes it; see [TDD](/learn/tdd)) where it can, at test seams agreed in advance. `/to-spec` checks those seams with you; on the short road, name them yourself when it asks. It closes with `/code-review`..." At the end of line 45, add: "The `/tdd` call can quietly not happen too, if no seams were agreed." Line 69 caption: "`/tdd` (at the agreed seams) and `/code-review` run inside." Cheat sheet row: "`/tdd` (at agreed seams), `/code-review` and `/pr` run for you".

accuracy.where: On-ramps, upkeep and side roads, line 187: "Three on-ramps bring in work that isn't your own idea, then merge onto the Main flow"
accuracy.problem: This is wrong for `/wayfinder`, the third on-ramp in the list. Wayfinder is for a loose idea too big and foggy to plan in one sitting, and that idea is usually your own (a greenfield project, a huge feature). ask-matt defines an on-ramp as a starting situation that generates work, not as work from someone else. A reader could decide a big idea of their own never belongs in `/wayfinder`.
accuracy.evidence: ask-matt/SKILL.md:44 'A starting situation that generates work, then merges onto the main flow.' ask-matt/SKILL.md:52 'A huge, foggy effort: a greenfield project or a huge feature build, too big for one session → /wayfinder'. wayfinder/SKILL.md:7 'A loose idea has arrived, too big for one agent session, and wrapped in fog'. The Lesson's own bullet at line 191 calls it 'A huge, foggy effort you can't even plan in one sitting'.
accuracy.fix: "Three on-ramps start from a situation rather than a sharp idea you can plan in one sitting (a pile of reports, a bug, an effort too foggy to map), then merge onto the Main flow:"
